text:
incident-bot: PAGER: perf.alert -> continuous-batcher (us-west-2)
- symptom: sustained p99 latency spike on continuous batching path
- timeframe: started 2026-03-14T08:15:01Z (~now), currently ongoing
- p95: 420ms -> 1.2s
- p99: 1.1s -> 3.2s
- streaming stalls observed: downstream clients reporting stalled tokens
dash: https://grafana.internal/redwood/boards/continuous-batcher?from=now-30m

alice_w: seeing the same in the traces. tails cluster c-batch-03 shows queue depth climbing, lots of mixed-seqlen batches hitting 512 max. :frowning:

ben_sre: acked. I'm on it. grabbing qps and node-level latencies. Can someone flag customer-facing apps?

cara_oncall: tagging @sam_ce and @eve_prod for customer impact. Sam, do we have any alerts from prod-support?

sam_ce: a couple customers (acme-inc, zoomlab) hit slow responses and 504s from our edge LB. CS already has a few tickets open. Not catastrophic yet but they see degraded throughput.

dave_p: quick triage: looks like continuous-batcher scheduler is producing very imbalanced batches because of mixed sequence-length distribution. small sequences get stuck behind a long sequence in a batch, KV cache misses spike, and streaming stalls when the long sequence dominates CPU bursts.

ben_sre: here's a quick query from metrics: 
```
avg_over_time(request_latency_ms{service="continuous-batcher",region="us-west-2"}[5m]) by (quantile)
```
p95 and p99 lines diverging around 08:10. Also saw a +30% variance in batch sizes across the pool.

alice_w: can we hot-fix by lowering max_batch_size and enabling preemptive-shedding on the path? There was a tuning flag `cbatch.max_batch_tokens` and `cbatch.shedding.enabled` we can flip.

cara_oncall: approved if it has been validated in staging. Ben / Dave, can you do a controlled change? We want minimal risk.

ben_sre: plan: 1) reduce `cbatch.max_batch_tokens` from 4096 -> 2048 on affected pool c-batch-02/03 2) enable `cbatch.shedding.enabled=true` 3) restart scheduler pods one at a time 4) monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall logs. Rolling deploy over 5m.

alice_w: please also add an override route to send time-sensitive traffic to model-variant `gptq-lite` fallback for 10% traffic. That will keep latency tight while we fix batching skew.

ben_sre: running the change now on c-batch-03 (canary). Command: 
```
kubectl patch cm cbatch-config -n inference -p '{"data":{"cbatch.max_batch_tokens":"2048","cbatch.shedding.enabled":"true"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/cbatch-scheduler -n inference --selector=pool=c-batch-03
```

ben_sre: canaries up. scheduler logs show batch sizes falling to median ~12 tokens vs previous ~24. p99 dropping in canary to ~1.4s. monitoring...

dave_p: good. Also pushing a change to the scheduler to prefer batching similar sequence-len together (soft affinity). It's a micro-change to the packer: add `seqlen_bucket` hashing. I'll stage it but not roll to prod until we confirm config changes help.

alice_w: Sam/Eve, can you draft a short status for CS and affected customers? Update: we have an ongoing mitigation (max_batch_tokens reduced, shedding enabled); partial relief observed in canary. ETA for full rollout 10-15m pending metrics.

sam_ce: on it. I'll send a PR to the incident status page and ping the open tickets.

cara_oncall: monitoring for regression: please watch for increased token cost or increased p50 — we don't want to blow cost. Also check retries from clients if they see 500/504 spikes during restarts.

ben_sre: rolling to c-batch-02 now. One pod at a time, 30s between restarts. Applying same config.

incident-bot: note -> incident created: INC-2026-0314-43 (severity: sev3). Pager duty: eng-oncall. Link: https://inc.internal/INC-2026-0314-43

alice_w: small gotcha: one pool had an older quantized kernel; when we restart it reverts to earlier kernel selection, causing transient latency. Ben, can you pin `kernel_version` in config to avoid that flip? Use `kernel: v2.3.1-patch` for now.

ben_sre: pinned kernel_version on updated pools. That was causing CPU jitter. Thanks for catching.
dave_p: can we add a short-term scheduler policy: if any batch has a token count > 3000 break it into two sub-batches immediately. Patch ready, will hold for after rollback testing.

ben_sre: full rollout done across c-batch-02/03. p95 now ~480ms, p99 ~820ms, streaming stalls significantly reduced. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher?from=now-15m

alice_w: nice. keeping it open for 30m observation window. Ben — please post rollout notes and config diffs to the change log. Also open a follow-up to evaluate automatic seqlen-bucketing in the scheduler and long-term mitigations (ticket: INF-2489).

sam_ce: status update posted to the incident page, notified affected customers. CS reports two customers happy with the mitigation; one still investigating client retry behavior.

eve_prod: small follow-up: logs show a handful of streaming clients timed out at 08:16:42 due to edge LB 504s. Those dropped requests were primarily hitting c-batch-03 before canary applied. No data loss but degraded UX.

cara_oncall: thanks everyone. we'll keep monitoring. If p99 settles under 1s for 30m we can demote to followup. Otherwise escalate.

ben_sre: logging post-mortem notes: root cause = scheduler packing policy not accounting for mixed sequence-length distribution; cascade: large seq tokens blocking batches -> KV cache churn -> CPU spikes -> streaming stalls. Mitigations applied: token cap, shedding, kernel pin, route fallback, plan for seqlen-bucketing.

alice_w: adding action items:
- INF-2489: implement seqlen-bucketing scheduler (priority P1)
- INF-2490: auto-shedding heuristics + config audit
- INF-2491: add alert for batch-token-skew and queue-depth per pool

cara_oncall: closing notes: incident remains open; monitoring window active until 2026-03-14T08:45:00Z. If stable, we'll convert to post-mortem and notify execs.

ben_sre: last check: p99 = 780ms, p95 = 460ms. Leaving traces sampling at 5x for next hour.

incident-bot: update -> incident INC-2026-0314-43 severity reduced to sev4 (mitigated), requires post-mortem and customer follow-ups.
